journey: Revise acquisition evidence and review contribution
expected: A newer UNKNOWN revision of a cost key invalidates that key's older known amount for current contribution; historical as-of queries may retain the earlier evidence.
actual: The January cost 200.01 is still used after a February UNKNOWN revision of the same key. The February summary reports contribution -103.04 and no missing inputs. _cost_evidence_rows filters UNKNOWN rows before choosing the latest version, resurrecting the superseded known row.
business_impact: A seller can receive a qualified profit/loss estimate based on acquisition evidence they explicitly marked unknown.
suggested_fix: Select the latest applicable cost revision first, then preserve UNKNOWN as a blocker; retain valid historical as-of behavior and cost lineage. Implement only with separate remediation authorization.

journey: Retry a stock movement without duplicating or misacknowledging it
expected: Identical retries return the original movement; conflicting delta or intent under the same key produces an explicit conflict rather than success for a different request.
actual: After recording delta 1, reusing the same key with delta 99 returns HTTP 200 and the original balance. Duplicate lookup checks only item/key, not movement identity. No extra stock was added; the defect is silent acceptance of conflicting intent.
business_impact: A seller or retrying client can believe a requested correction succeeded although a different earlier movement was returned.
suggested_fix: Define canonical semantic replay identity and reject changed movement payloads while retaining identical retry and concurrency safety.

journey: Record and safely retry sale/refund evidence
expected: An existing source event ID must not acknowledge materially different monetary evidence as an identical replay.
actual: Replaying the recorded sale with amount 999999 returns HTTP 201/idempotent true and the old event. Both preflight and uniqueness-recovery paths return the existing event without checking amount/type/reference identity. Existing data is not overwritten.
business_impact: Conflicting sale or refund evidence can be silently discarded while a client sees a success response, obscuring reconciliation errors.
suggested_fix: Compare normalized authoritative event identity in both replay paths and return a conflict for changed evidence, without weakening identical-delivery deduplication.

journey: Acknowledge then resolve a signal with traceable HUMAN intent
expected: A resolve request cannot reuse an acknowledge key and receive a successful response for the earlier transition.
actual: A resolve request using the acknowledge key returns HTTP 200, the old transition ID and ACKNOWLEDGED state. _transition looks up owner/key but does not compare signal, target state or note.
business_impact: The displayed/requested HUMAN intent and audit transition may disagree, making operational review unreliable.

evidence.name: Resolve acknowledged as the old transition

suggested_fix: Validate semantic transition scope and target under the canonical owner/key lock; preserve identical concurrent replays.

journey: Replenish stock and refresh operational guidance
expected: A rescan after stock recovery must retire or explicitly stale the obsolete out-of-stock claim; acknowledgement alone does not make old evidence current.
actual: After the same item is replenished from 0 to 20 and rescanned, its signal remains ACKNOWLEDGED/critical with evidence available 0, source version v1 and confidence 0.90. The scan upserts current matches but does not invalidate no-longer-matching signals.
business_impact: A seller may waste time or make unnecessary replenishment decisions from a high-confidence obsolete recommendation. No automatic procurement was executed.
reproduction_steps: Inspect test_15_source_changes_rescan_and_signal_resolution and the preceding stock adjustment.

evidence.name: Old source claim after replenishment and rescan

suggested_fix: Reconcile emitted fingerprints against current source state, retaining history while transitioning obsolete claims to a truthful noncurrent state. Do not auto-approve any business action.

journey: Distinguish rehearsal data from real marketplace evidence
expected: Financial fallback from fake-provider orders remains explicitly synthetic, even when no separate financial event exists.
actual: The Flipkart summary contains only fake orders, canonical_order_fallback true and event_count 0, but synthetic_provider false. The flag inspects FinancialEvent source_type only and ignores fake order totals/provenance. The UI uses this flag to choose Synthetic fixture versus Canonical evidence.
business_impact: A rehearsal can be presented as non-synthetic financial evidence, undermining trust in seller readiness and forecasts.

evidence.name: Fake-order fallback with false synthetic flag

suggested_fix: Propagate synthetic/trust provenance through every contributing canonical source, never promote missing source classification to real/verified evidence.

journey: Resolve and reopen persisted seller work
expected: Selecting Resolved retrieves and displays persisted resolved signals with useful history.
actual: After resolving a card, choosing Resolved shows no card although the detail API reports RESOLVED and history. The select updates ngModel only; load() requests include_resolved only when called later, so the current dataset excludes resolved rows. Reproduced on desktop/mobile.
business_impact: Sellers cannot reliably find completed work through the offered status filter and may think their review history was lost.
reproduction_steps: QA-P3-04: acknowledge and resolve the browser warning, then choose Resolved without another refresh.

evidence.name: Browser screenshots, trace and API proof

suggested_fix: Trigger an authoritative reload on the status change and keep loading/error/context feedback; do not remove the filter or relax the browser assertion.

journey: Reopen the exact calculation used before a later refund or cost revision
expected: If historical calculation review is offered, earlier metrics and complete input lineage can be reconstructed; otherwise explicitly document that only current projections are supported.
actual: The supported authority overwrites one calculation row per scope/version. A later refund keeps the ID but changes metrics; the list is current projections, not immutable versions. Lineage lists event IDs but not the cost evidence used. This is a missing workflow, not a broken existing immutable-history contract. The final test validates the actual mutable contract.
business_impact: A seller cannot reconstruct the exact earlier profitability calculation from this projection alone, even though source events remain persisted.
suggested_fix: Define whether retained calculation versions are required; reuse canonical snapshot/audit patterns and include applicable cost/source identities. Do not relabel current projections as immutable history.

journey: Turn an advisory signal into an explicitly reviewed supported action
expected: Distinguish signal acknowledgement from a durable canonical HUMAN approval; do not claim approval or execution where only an advisory response exists.
actual: The request-action authority returns approval_required and says the recommendation is recorded, but it adds no durable approval/action record. There is no approve/reject/failed-execution/retry lifecycle in this authority. The default-deny external boundary is working and was not bypassed.
business_impact: A first-time seller may mistake a requested or acknowledged signal for a saved authorization or completed action.
suggested_fix: Clarify messaging and route only supported actions to their existing canonical HUMAN authorities; do not add a duplicate approval system or expose remote execution in QA.

journey: Create a first stock record from the inventory empty state
expected: An inventory empty state gives a supported UI path to create the canonical item before adjustments, reservations and channel mapping.
actual: The workspace tells the seller to create a product stock record, but exposes filters, adjustments, ledger and mapping only for existing items. Its canonical creation API exists; this suite seeds it through that API. Product master inventory fields are a separate model and are not a demonstrated replacement for this missing handoff.
business_impact: API fixtures can exercise populated inventory, but a first-time seller can still encounter a UI onboarding dead end.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the empty state and controls in unified-inventory.component.ts
Compare POST /api/v1/inventory/items with MarketplaceService UI callers.
suggested_fix: Plan an explicit canonical creation/handoff using the existing API, with opening balance provenance and HUMAN review. Do not duplicate stock ledgers.

journey: Read due-diligence, economic and financial evidence on mobile
expected: Every relevant visible caption and table cell can be evaluated without claiming obscured or incomplete contrast checks as passes.
actual: All 107 original repeated-state target occurrences were examined after real scrolling using axe. 101 passed and six caption occurrences remain incomplete; no contrast violation was confirmed. A separate financial-loss screen also retains four incomplete mobile nodes. These are manual-review tasks, not confirmed WCAG failures and not resolved findings.
business_impact: Automated testing cannot yet establish readability of every mobile caption/obscured table element; first-time seller comprehension and assistive-technology behavior still need review.
reproduction_steps: Inspect QA-P3-06 scrolling diagnostics and QA-P3-03 full-document axe findings on mobile.
suggested_fix: Manually review clipped captions and table reading/keyboard behavior, then authorize a focused responsive/accessibility correction if needed. Retain full-document axe checks and do not suppress incomplete results.
